questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses, the language in the country and the nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing student city and talented teachers.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was incredible difficult and annoying to plan the trip. Everytime i tried contacting someone, they would often send me on to another person. It would have been amazing, if there has been a number to call to who could help explain everything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a presentation from a teacher and got emails containing information about the place and who to contact if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Everything was okay simpel and people were helpfull.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The Housing office made it very easy to find house accomodations.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If they choose to live at Flogsta, it should be for the social life and not the acommodations. The social life is amazing, but the buildings are old and incredible dirty.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Definetely think about if you want to be social in your home also and not just your studies. Living in a dorm and especially Flogsta was the best decision i could have made. I gained many friendships from that place.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not easy at all, but with many extra calls i succeeded.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was complicated and i was in contact with many different people. I succeeded in the end.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses i wanted in the end, but the way there was horrible and very long.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Call them and ask for an explanation in how their courses works (if they are different from your own home university).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Incredible teachers and no lack of resources. Really an amazing experience to be tought at Uppsala University.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 3 courses with 7, 10 and 15 ECTS.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different and much more physical than i was used to. Many excursions and changes in teaching methods.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Marine biology 15 ECTS
Natural science and religion 7 ECTS 
Faunistics vertebrates 10 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Marine biology 15 ECTS and Faunistics vertebrates 10 ECTS. 
For someone interested in the zoology part of biology, these courses were absolutely brilliant and with talented teachers. The teaching methods were mixed and there was a lot of excursions and practicals.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Buying a bike and a couple of things for the housing. Very expensive alcohol.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Vegetables are incredible expensive, together with alcohol.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The nations were the best part.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of student nations with a vast variation of activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Working in a student nation (for the social connections). 
Going on hikes in the nature (there are cabins all around that people can sleep in for free).
Try to learn the language.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking, working in student nations, visit cities nearby and take advantage of the many activities in student nations.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Socializing with sweds is not as easy as internationals. They are very private, but working at student nations is a good way to socialize.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sweds are very private and afraid of conflicst - and can be very rude to Danish people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Politeness and the acceptance of different sexualities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be afraid to ask someone if you can join an activity. 
Ask people out on fika as much as possible and take advantage of the activities in the student nations.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not take to many courses if possible and especially be sure to look at the percentage of the course that you have chosen. Figuring out the courses can be tricky, but it is good to take some interesting courses, but on 50% or 33%. The social activites every week can be very hard to balance with courses that are on 100%.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends for life, learning about independence and evolving my skills within zoology.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning to listen to when I needed a break from the social activities and to balance studying with the social student life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Uppsala is a perfect and amazing city to be a student in.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
